title: Expected distribution
view: Shared front-view base (visuals/distribution_bases/front): skeleton on the left, grey body on the right, patient's right on the image left; right-sided block.
teachingPoint: An interscalene block numbs the shoulder and lateral upper arm and the radial forearm, plus the cape of the shoulder; the ulnar side and the hand are spared.
claims: Skin (teal): deltoid and lateral arm (axillary nerve), radial half of the forearm to the wrist (musculocutaneous, C5-C7).

Skin (violet): the cape of the shoulder and the skin over the clavicle (supraclavicular nerves, C3-C4), reached by spread to the superficial cervical plexus; the legend states it is spread, not the target.

Bone: shoulder joint, humerus and lateral clavicle with the acromion. Not shaded: the ulnar border of the forearm and the hand (the lower trunk is usually spared; the radial hand is C6-C7 but not reliably covered), the elbow and below.
Right-sided block, patient's right on the image left (house laterality); one tone per nerve, key shown under the image in the app.

geometry.why: skeleton on the left, body on the right
